title: Answers of the bot on a second corpus, scope B

corpus.label: scope B
corpus.description: security procedures of a manufacturing company (PDF, scans, Office)
corpus.formats: text PDFs, scanned PDFs, Word, Excel, slide decks of training courses with speaker notes

sample.how: 59 questions written by Claude Sonnet from the documents, 40 from the quizzes of the company's training courses, 20 with no answer in the documents

judges.model: Claude Opus, through the claude plugin (reference variant only)

judge_rules: score from -10 to +10 with a reason; the judge reads the question, the expected answer, the bot's answer and the sources given to the bot (up to 18,000 characters)
"I don't know" scores 0; information taken from the sources is not invented; leaving something out is not an error
good: score of 7 or more; wrong: below 0; the score of an answer is the mean of gemma4 and qwen3; Claude's scores are reported apart

gpu_host.use: every model: embeddings, reranker, answers, judges, image descriptions, OCR models
gpu_host.rule: everything stays in the 16 GB of VRAM, nothing offloaded to the CPU

cpu_host.use: gosidian, the plugins, Qdrant and PostgreSQL, the converters that run on the CPU

config: the reference configuration of scope A: paragraphs in Qdrant, Qwen3-Embedding-8B at 2048, ef 128, bge-reranker-v2-m3 on 20 candidates, k 5, the section as context, images in place, gemma4:12b with 12,288 tokens

variants.label: without the courses
variants.change: the five slide decks of the training courses left out

notes: score, good, wrong, precise, broad: from the mean of gemma4 and qwen3 per answer; Claude's score is reported apart. With Claude as a third judge the reference variant scores 8.57 (precise 8.62, broad 7.17, wrong 2%)
documents converted with the docling plugin; the five slide decks with a script that keeps one section per slide with the speaker notes, the output docling 0.4.0 has since adopted
the training courses matter: the questions from their quizzes drop from 8.84 to 6.71 without them

by topic (with the courses, mean of the local judges) six groups score 8.1-9.7; the lowest, risk assessment, scores 4.9: 5 of its 8 questions are answered by data in the tables and charts of one PDF, a case for the conversion benchmark
Claude is stricter on broad questions (6.09 against 7.72 of the local judges); 119 scores took 10 minutes and about 28% of a five-hour usage window of a Claude subscription
